0.why: bitter.cpp:80 reads this input with getVoltage, which is channel 0 only
bitter.cpp:96 writes this output with setVoltage and no channel index, from a byte mapped back onto -1 to 1 and multiplied by 5

comment: The input is mapped to an unsigned byte at bitter.cpp:80 and back at bitter.cpp:94. The three switch positions are read as 2 for up (no change), 1 for centre (clear the bit) and 0 for down (toggle the bit) at bitter.cpp:84 to :91, which matches the README. Each line is written for the switch that was clicked; the bit each one controls is given in the panel numbering, switch 1 being the least significant.
